brief: id: "harbor-run". name: "Harbor Run". Theme: a sunlit coastal harbour, the first track a new player sees. Target total length about 1400 m. Character: the easiest track in the game. Wide and forgiving throughout, 20-22 m on the straights. Four or five long sweeping corners and one gentle chicane, no hairpins, no dirt. Elevation almost flat, within 6 m of 0, with one shallow rise over a bridge near the middle of the lap. Two boost pads on the two longest straight exits. One short ramp on the back straight with a launch of about 5. Item boxes in wide rows of 5. This track should be impossible to fall off.

id: "dust-canyon". name: "Dust Canyon". Theme: a dry desert canyon with a loose river bed cutting through it. Target total length about 1650 m. Character: medium difficulty, and the game's introduction to a loose surface. Roughly a fifth of the lap - one contiguous run of control points, not scattered ones - uses surface "dirt" for the river bed section, narrowing to about 15 m there. The rest is tarmac at 17-20 m. Two medium-radius corners bank hard. Elevation drops about 14 m into the canyon and climbs back out over the lap, changing gradually. Two ramps on the canyon floor with launches around 7 and 9. Boost pads placed to reward taking the dirt line cleanly.

id: "neon-district". name: "Neon District". Theme: a rain-slick city at night, cutting between tower blocks. Target total length about 1250 m. Character: the technical track. Tight and busy - two hairpins, three 90-degree street corners, and a short chicane. Narrower than the others at 14-16 m on the straights, opening to 20 m through the hairpins so there is a passing line. All tarmac. Elevation nearly flat, within 5 m. No ramps at all. Four boost pads on the corner exits, because exit speed is the whole skill of this track. Use 14 or more checkpoints so the tight sequence cannot be cut.

id: "redwood-rise". name: "Redwood Rise". Theme: a forest road climbing and falling through enormous trees. Target total length about 1800 m, the longest track in the game. Character: medium difficulty, defined entirely by elevation. The lap climbs about 22 m over its first half and descends over its second, changing gradually and never more than 3 m between consecutive points. Long flowing corners, one long downhill straight, one uphill hairpin. Mostly tarmac at 18-21 m with a short dirt section where the road crosses a clearing. One ramp at the bottom of the descent with a launch of about 10. Item boxes concentrated on the climb, where players need them.

id: "caldera". name: "Caldera". Theme: a volcanic crater rim with a lava field in the middle. Target total length about 1500 m. Character: hard, and the most dramatic. The lap runs around a crater rim, so it is close to circular in plan but with three deliberate direction changes that break the rhythm. Heavy banking, up to the 0.35 limit, on the two fastest corners. Elevation rises and falls about 18 m around the rim. Width 16-19 m, narrowing to 15 m at the rim's high point where it is most exposed. Mostly tarmac with a short dirt run through an ash drift. Three ramps, the largest with a launch of about 12. Only two boost pads - speed is already the danger here.

id: "glacier-pass". name: "Glacier Pass". Theme: a wide ice shelf cut by a meltwater channel. Target total length about 1550 m. Character: hard in a different way from Caldera - fast and wide open, where the difficulty is carrying speed rather than precision. Very wide at 21-26 m throughout, with three enormous high-speed sweepers and one genuinely slow hairpin at the far end to break the flow. All tarmac. Elevation gently descending then climbing, within 10 m. Two ramps over the meltwater channel with launches around 6 and 8. Boost pads on the sweeper exits. Because the track is so wide, place item boxes in rows of 5 spread far apart laterally.
